name: Stanford HAI AI Index landing page: annual macro data on AI
title: Stanford HAI AI Index landing page: annual macro data on AI
answer: The Stanford HAI AI Index page introduces an independent annual report that tracks, collates, distills, and visualizes data on artificial intelligence for policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the public. Its most useful claim is that this year's Index finds a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared we are to manage it, even as technical capabilities improve, investment accelerates, and adoption spreads. The page says the report offers a comprehensive, cross sector view of AI's technical progress, economic influence, and societal impact.

sections.body: Stanford HAI publishes this page for the AI Index, an independent initiative at the Stanford Institute for Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence. It is a landing page for an annual report, not the report itself. The page states that the seventh edition is the 2024 Index and describes the program as a collaborative effort led by the AI Index Steering Committee, an interdisciplinary group from academia and industry. Its stated scope is to track, collate, distill, and visualize data on artificial intelligence for policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the general public.
sections.heading: What this source is

sections.body: The page says the AI Index mission is to provide unbiased, rigorously vetted, and globally sourced data so that policymakers, researchers, journalists, executives, and the general public can develop a deeper understanding of the complex field of AI. It tracks, collates, distills, and visualizes data relating to artificial intelligence. This year's Index, according to the page, reveals a widening gap between what AI can do and how prepared we are to manage it. AI continues its rapid integration into the global economy, with technical capabilities improving, investment accelerating, and adoption spreading, but the frameworks needed to govern, evaluate, and understand the technology are falling behind. In a field where data transparency is declining, the page argues that independent, rigorous measurement has never been more critical, and it calls the report the most comprehensive analysis of AI's trajectory available. Stanford HAI says AI is poised to be the most transformative technology of the 21st century, but its benefits will not be evenly distributed unless development is guided thoughtfully. The page says the AI Index is recognized globally and cited in major newspapers including The New York Times, Bloomberg, and The Guardian, with hundreds of academic citations and references by high level policymakers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. It says this year's edition surpasses previous ones in size, scale, and scope. The program writes about AI progress and impact through a cross sector lens, from research and development to technical performance, the economy, education, policy.
sections.heading: What it says

sections.body: The page states that this is the seventh edition and that the 2024 Index is the most comprehensive to date. It says previous editions have been cited in The New York Times, Bloomberg, and The Guardian, have amassed hundreds of academic citations, and have been referenced by high level policymakers in the United States, the United Kingdom, and the European Union. It also mentions a fall 2019 Stanford workshop paper that identifies six summary challenges in measuring AI progress and impact and summarizes over 40 presentations. It gives no nonprofit specific figures.
sections.heading: Figures and claims worth noting

sections.body: A reader following AI in nonprofits would use this page as a citable macro source for AI's technical progress, economic influence, and societal impact, which the page says the AI Index covers through a cross sector lens including education and policy. It can supply context for funding, governance, and adoption trends that affect mission driven work, but the page itself does not discuss nonprofits or offer nonprofit specific data. It is best treated as background on the wider AI landscape rather than evidence about nonprofit implementation.
sections.heading: What it means for AI in Nonprofits

sections.body: This is a landing page for the AI Index, not the full report, so it does not provide the underlying data, methodology, or detailed findings. It does not mention nonprofits or mission driven organizations. The page is partly promotional, describing the Index as credible and authoritative and asking for philanthropic support. It refers to the seventh edition and the 2024 Index, and it mentions a 2019 workshop, so parts of the material are dated. It is published by Stanford HAI, an academic initiative, and its scope is broad rather than sector specific.
